# Damage sharing, prevention and interception

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED —39 exact source passages and two supporting Tinker engine passages.** [Final notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_REDIRECTION_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) closes this bounded damage-sharing interface with94 checks and186 conservation states. It does not establish every item/spell defense, companion lifecycle, all-source attack chain or numerical balance. Original source cards remain unchanged.

Read the [source register](REDIRECTION_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md), [source checks](REDIRECTION_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [reference checks](REDIRECTION_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json), [first notebook proposal](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_REDIRECTION_FIRST_REVIEW_PARTIAL.md) and [complete corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_REDIRECTION_BOUNDARIES.md). Later corrections supersede the retained first proposal.

## Resolve the kind of protection first

Guardian Pulse changes the target of an attack before comparing its original roll with AC. The Guardian becomes the actual hit/miss and on-hit-rider target. One attack can be retargeted once. Multiple offers are chosen by the original intended target; only the selected Guardian spends its Reaction/use. After the incoming attack fully resolves, a surviving, eligible Guardian may make the printed counterattack against an attacker in reach whether the original attack hit or missed. This free attack cannot grant another free attack or Action. Retargeting does not spend the later damage-transfer opportunity.

Bloodbond and Veinlock Tether divide the finalized raw damage before either recipient's mitigation. Attack/save success, save-halving and critical dice have already determined that amount. Bloodbond transfers one quarter, rounded down; Veinlock instead chooses up to S+M. Each recipient applies its own eligible defenses once to its own share.

Other supplied damage transfers divide damage after the original target's defenses and legal pure prevention, before temporary HP. Their transferred portions keep damage type and skip another DR/resistance/immunity/prevention stage. Temporary HP, applicable HP floors, would-die replacements, Wounds, concentration and ordinary life consequences still apply. “Unmitigated damage” does not mean “death cannot be prevented.”

Pure prevention removes damage without creating a second recipient. Elemental Absorption adds its resistance during ordinary defenses. Aura of Bonds and Crown reductions use the strongest applicable class flat reduction, then resistance/immunity. Finite/reactive prevention such as Bloom and Ancestral Guardian follows those defenses before post-defense transfer and temporary HP. Verify additional item/spell sources before treating this as universal defense ordering.

Redirecting Palm prevents half the Monk's post-defense damage, rounded down. The Monk keeps the remainder. A second enemy distinct from the triggering melee attacker, within5feet, can receive new force damage equal to the prevented amount, capped at Monk level. That new damage gets its own defenses; it is not a transferred attack or critical hit. With no second enemy, the Monk still receives the reduction.

Direct HP payments from Blood Sacrifice, Flesh-to-RP, Profane Exchange and Channel Life stay outside the damage sequence. They bypass temporary HP, obey their own legal minimum HP and do not create damage/Wound/resource triggers from paying the cost. Healing-recipient substitution and excess-healing conversion also remain distinct operations.

## One transfer operation and exact amounts

A root here means one original recipient's damage packet. A shared area cast has a separate root for each original recipient, under the same cast/roll identity.

One such root accepts one damage-sharing operation across all owners. A pre-mitigation split locks both its retained original portion and transferred portions against later transfer. Burden Shared can divide one operation among up to two other explicitly willing recipients. It does not create two redirection events. No transferred recipient may be the original damage target.

**New stage-precedence integration:** consider pre-mitigation offers before applying defenses, and post-defense offers afterward. Within the same stage, select eligible positive mandatory/automatic protection before optional offers; competing mandatory claims are chosen by the original damage target. A legally chosen Bloodbond/Veinlock operation can therefore preempt later Aegis/Final Stand because that root is already claimed. Do not preview or consume defenses/Bloom to decide a later-stage preference. The helper accepts an already selected legal operation; it does not select Reactions or schedule automatic offers.

Optional transfer requires a positive chosen amount and available damage. Zero transfer cannot spend an optional Reaction/resource/use. A mandatory rounded-zero share does nothing and spends no transfer allowance. An independently legal prevention component can still occur.

| Source | Transferred amount |
|---|---|
| Bloodbond | floor(raw damage/4), fixed |
| Veinlock Tether / Shared Breath / Selfless Guardian | chosen up to S+M |
| Protective Stance / Emergency Protocols | min(S+M, available damage), fixed |
| Life Linked | chosen up to floor(available damage/2) |
| Guardian Tissue | floor(available damage/3), fixed |
| Aegis Incarnate / Martyr's Share | floor(available damage/2), fixed |
| Chainbound Smite | chosen up to max(3, actual CHA modifier) |
| Linked Ward | chosen up to max(2, twice actual CHA modifier) |
| King's Smite protection | chosen up to5 |
| Aura of the Crown | chosen up to M |
| Crown of Embers / Burden Shared | chosen up to level+M |
| Crown Undying | chosen up to remaining level+M round allowance |
| Final Stand | all available damage, subject to shared allowance |

Every amount is capped by the available packet at its source's stage. Fixed fractions/fixed protection cannot voluntarily choose a smaller amount. Original actions, range, willingness, costs, active-state requirements, cadence and source-specific use limits still apply.

## Hit identity and final damage accounting

The original damage target retains its original hit, failed-save, critical and on-hit-rider identity even if all damage is transferred. A rider that requires positive damage must recheck the actual remaining packet. A transferred recipient was not hit by that attack and did not fail its save; it receives no attached poison/control/maiming/knockout rider merely because damage moved.

Accordingly, transferred damage from a critical attack gives an already0HP recipient the ordinary one damage failure, not two critical-hit failures. Concentration still sees the transferred recipient's resolved packet even if temporary HP absorbs all of it.

Use the [reviewed life-state interface](HEALING_DEATH_PLAYTEST.md) after resolving each final recipient. Numeric actual damage is temporary HP absorbed plus actual normal HP lost, excluding overkill and damage prevented by an HP floor. Sum each terminal recipient once. Do not also count the unsplit parent or unrelated counterdamage.

Physical root totals include every recipient. A healing/resource/reflection consumer sums only branches permitted for that consumer and qualifying for its own source's target predicate. For example, a meaningful-hostile-only drain does not automatically count damage transferred onto a friendly protector. Check all applicable flags for a compound trigger, such as a passive healing proc.

## Source-specific restrictions

All transfers prohibit another transfer. All supplied post-defense transfers prohibit another mitigation/prevention stage. Further restrictions differ:

| Source family | Additional restrictions on transferred damage |
|---|---|
| Paladin engine | No reflection or resource generation; does not universally prohibit other retaliation or healing |
| Protective Stance | Also no generic damage-trigger chains |
| Burden Shared | Also no derived healing |
| Oracle Life Linked | No reflection, resource/RC, passive, condition, action or copy generation; no recovery or retaliation |
| Guardian Tissue / Aegis | No BT generation; no invented ban on every other resource |
| Shared Breath | No additional generic trigger prohibition |
| Selfless Guardian / Emergency Protocols | No retaliation chain |
| Bloodbond / Veinlock | Each recipient still has its one defense stage; no additional blanket prohibition |

A no-derived-healing flag does not prevent unrelated later healing of the recipient.

The source's explicit redirection riders remain narrowly available. Unbroken Covenant triggers on the redirection operation, even when Protective Stance prohibits generic damage triggers; use half the final protector actual damage, capped at S+M. These self-absorption riders require damage actually transferred to the redirecting owner, not to another ally under Burden Shared. Linked Ward's own transfer granting temporary HP on reducing the Paladin to0 uses final actual damage, capped at level+M. Final Stand also gives the protected ally temporary HP equal to Paladin level and resistance to all damage through that ally's next turn end; the numeric helper handles only temporary HP, and the caller must create the resistance record. None grants a generic permission to ignore other source restrictions. Temporary HP still uses the larger remaining amount and does not stack.

## Paladin round ledger

Track each Paladin owner's numbered-round events. Ordinarily, one redirection event is available, using exactly one Paladin redirection feature. Final Stand is automatic on the first eligible positive post-defense packet while its allowance remains; the Paladin cannot save it for a later hit. Its “all damage” text does not override the explicit engine ceiling. It may redirect again in a later numbered round if still active before its source-next-start deadline.

Crown Undying can raise the owner's total to two different damage events, with at most one ordinary/non-Crown feature. The additional permission belongs to Crown Undying. A prior ordinary redirection remains recorded if Crown activates later in the same round; only one further Crown event is then possible. Reapplication does not clear history.

The two Crown events may protect the same selected ally. Sum Crown-transferred amounts against level+M per round. Its heal is floor(final Paladin branch actual damage/2) for each event, then capped by the remaining S+M per protected ally that round. Commit that nominal source entitlement before target healing restrictions; blocked or capped healing refunds no event, transfer amount or healing entitlement. The heal cannot heal the Paladin or start another redirection/heal-copy chain.

## Bloom and devices

Bloom Ward is a finite10+Oracle-level prevention pool across packets. Apply its legal prevention after ordinary defenses. Subtract only the prevented amount. The bloom ends on depletion, its1minute expiry, or actual legal removal. Suppression alone does not end it. Ending grants the printed +1 Frightened-save rider through the target's next end. A late clock observation must retain the endpoint calculated from the actual expiry, not create a fresh duration. An unmitigated transferred branch cannot consume this prevention pool.

Emergency Protocols requires an active/conscious drone within its printed range. The transfer occurs after the Tinker's defenses and before temporary HP. The drone receives the bounded transferred amount without mitigation; legally granted temporary HP can absorb it. At0HP the drone is destroyed and receives no organic Wound or death-save procedure.

Tinker engine[2] retains the destroyed drone at0 until its explicit repair/rebuild procedure. Ordinary functional repair cannot reconstruct a destroyed drone or reset ammunition, uses, duration or command budget. This package's device helper only resolves damage/destruction; it does not implement reconstruction or grant a destruction reward. The broader companion/device lifecycle remains open.

## Reference boundary

The helper validates arithmetic, stages, branch identity, replay protection and round entitlements. Callers establish legal sources, target relationships, exact source cadence, action/resource payment, clock endpoints and source-native riders. No helper imports card ownership merely from a string identifier. The source register preserves every exact original procedure alongside the overlay.

Guardian Pulse's new counterattack carries its explicit no-further-free-attack/no-Action limits, without inheriting unrelated incoming healing/resource/reflection restrictions. Palm's force damage has no invented copy/action/resource prohibition; each downstream source determines eligibility. It cannot trigger another Palm because it is not a melee attack.

Validation currently covers94 targeted checks and186 conservation states. Full-game completion, human balance and all-source combat/device execution remain separate unfinished work.

# Healing, survival and resurrection — playtest interface

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED — selected scope only.** The [final notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) closes147 classified class passages plus6 individually reviewed ordinary spell objects. [Exact source procedures](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) · [Latest boundary decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_BOUNDARIES.md) · [Supplement decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_SUPPLEMENT_REVIEW.md) · [Reference checks](HEALING_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) · [Source integrity](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json)

## Distinct life operations

| Operation | Result | Restriction interface |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum-HP prevention | Preserve positiveHP instead of crossing a floor | Not HP gain; cannot create positiveHP from0 |
| Ordinary healing | Increase a living creature's normalHP | Apply modifiers, prohibitions, reserve and Critical ceiling |

## Damage quantities and resolution

| Quantity | Definition and use |

| resolvedDamage | After defenses, before tempHP; positive damage event iff greater than0 |
| tempAbsorbed | min(tempHP, resolvedDamage) |
| postTempDamage | resolvedDamage minus tempAbsorbed, uncapped by currentHP; Core Instant Death/Wounds |
| actualHpDamage | NormalHP lost to the packet after true prevention; recovery and state-assignment loss excluded |

Numeric actual-damage wording (Sanguine Rite/Echo Leech/Merciful Smite/Wound Eater/Gravebrand) uses actualDamageDealt. Source attack/hit predicates remain distinct.

Example: HP10/temp10 takes5: numeric actual damage5, actualHP damage0, positive packet. HP1 under a floor takes5: numeric0 but positive packet. HP3 takes12: numeric3, raw post-temp12. HP0 takes1: numeric0, positive packet and normal death-failure consequences.

Thus HP1-floor/numeric0 reflects1 and consumes; fully prevented resolved0 does neither. Wrathful Brand/Balanced Scales use the positive predicate where their source says damage occurred.

Resolve a damage event in this order:

1. Snapshot pre-event HP/tempHP/Wounds; resolve defenses, temp absorption and uncapped post-temp damage.
2. Core Instant Death uses postTempDamage minus preHP greater than or equal to effective maximum when reduced to0. It precedes ordinary floors. Open a legal would-die replacement; stop that packet's death procedure. No Wound save or zero-HP failure follows this branch.
3. If not Instant Death, resolve applicable true floors. They cannot raise an already0 creature. They preserve raw damage and attached conditions; a prevented drop creates no drop-only Wound trigger, but half-max/Maiming still applies.

The affected creature chooses among simultaneously eligible offered survival effects, then rechecks remaining triggers. A paid Reaction spends its declared cost; a limited automatic survival use spends when its actual source resolves. A true floor preventing the crossing means Spiral's use is not spent. For Ritual Ward, sufficient body and no explicitly unpreventable death are prerequisites. # Forms and temporary HP

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED — selected form and temporary-HP interfaces.** This overlay covers 175 exact source roles, five support passages, 26 Druid form profiles and selected common interfaces. GPT approved the corrected reference and its clock-initialization addendum; 165 contract checks and 1,053 shield/damage scenarios pass. It does not close full class cards, feats, ancestry, ordinary spell catalogs, equipment or the whole game. Original cards and historical text remain unchanged in the [source register](FORM_TEMP_HP_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md). Use the [Druid form quick reference](DRUID_FORM_QUICK_REFERENCE.md) for the compact form and special-cost tables.

## One active shield

Temporary HP is a single active grant with its own identity, source, owner, recipient, remaining points, endpoint and explicitly attached permissions. A larger new offer replaces it; a smaller or equal offer is discarded. Equal values preserve the existing grant and its deadline. Discarded shields do not remain underneath. A rejected offer cannot lend its duration or linked rider to the winner. A zero offer creates no grant.

Pay the legal source's printed costs before comparing shields. Costs are not refunded because the new shield loses. Druid Buffer Reserve pays the entire offered amount, not just the increase over an existing shield. Preflight actual source access, targets, geometry, actions, components and resources before paying anything; illegal activations spend nothing.

Unless the source states a different shield lifetime, a grant ends at the recipient's next completed long rest. “Until lost” or “until lost or replaced” only restates depletion; it does not exempt a grant from that default. Explicit fixed deadlines and source dependencies take precedence, even when they outlast a long rest. An ongoing ability's general duration does not automatically shorten an instantaneous shield that it generates.

Temporary HP absorbs post-defense damage before normal HP. It is not healing: it cannot stabilize, revive, wake an Unconscious creature, remove Wounds, reset death counters or pay direct/sacrificial HP costs. A living creature at0 can receive it without gaining any of those benefits. A dead body is not a valid holder. A prohibition on HP healing does not implicitly prohibit a separately legal shield.

## Exact endpoints and riders

Use actual owner/recipient regular-turn markers, absolute deadlines and encounter identities, not extra-turn or copied clocks. Source-specific rules remain in the exact card; this table resolves the important ambiguities.

| Source | Shield endpoint / linked boundary |
|---|---|
| Crimson Bloodshield | End of its three owner turns. Its one Reaction is attached only to its accepted grant; depletion/replacement/expiry removes permission. |
| Bloodbond; Lingering Malice | Each trigger/pulse makes a default long-rest grant; ending concentration does not erase it. |
| Nature's Blessing; Dread Shelter; Nano-Aegis command | Start/cast/command shield uses default long-rest lifetime; Speed, DR and support mode keep their separate clocks. |
| Protective Programming | Offer before the triggering hit. Resolve that hit, then remove any remainder of this particular grant. A stronger unrelated shield that won comparison is unaffected. |
| Monk Support; Warder Arrow and capstone | Default long-rest grants. Permanent availability or an instantaneous attack is not a permanent shield. |
| Harmonized Core; Arcane Leech; Primordial Surge; King's Smite; Noble Bearing | Default long-rest lifetime, including the sources that merely say “until lost.” |
| Linked Ward | After the actual triggering packet, default long-rest grant. |
| Final Stand | After actual triggering packet; shield and triggered resistance end at the ally's next regular end. The redirection itself ends at the Paladin's next regular start. **New grammatical integration.** |
| Unbroken Covenant | Until the Lock ends; this clause is explicit in preserved source provenance. |
| Last King's Gift | After damage, until encounter end. Its existing death-prevention gate remains separate. |
| Soldier Rally Point | Shield until encounter end; next-save bonus only until Soldier's next regular start. |
| Soldier Rallying Cry | Encounter end. |
| Dragoon Bastion Descent | Shield until Dragoon's next regular start; resistance until used or that start; cleanse instantaneous. **New grammatical integration.** |
| Bear / Earth Warden | Bound to that form instance; no refill at renewal. |
| Mooncursed ally Howl | Independent default long-rest grants, surviving Druid reversion. **New bridge clarification.** |
| Overflowing Light | Original two-round endpoint; if this exact grant is still active with at least1 point, allow ending one actual Frightened, Poisoned or Staggered condition. Rejection, replacement, depletion or holder/dependency removal gives no cleanse. Mastery raises only the cap10→20. |
| Protective Verse | One-minute shield and a separate one-minute next-qualifying-save rider. The rider can survive shield replacement. |
| Arcane Sanctuary | Each accepted pulse until owner's next regular start or source end, whichever first. Its attack bonus is a separate zone effect. |
| Empowered Link | Half the eligible source numeric benefit, rounded down/minimum1 where applicable; shared benefit duration capped at owner's next regular end. It cannot share resources, Actions, resistance or other excluded effects. |

Other explicit minute, round, turn and encounter endpoints retain their exact source wording. Cleric return shields, Crimson Pact, Mirrorsage Ward profiles, Mage Resonance Shield and Soulbound use their printed one-minute deadlines. Light Binding ends at owner's next regular end. Momentum Shield, Bolstering Presence, Aura Surge, Black Manifestation, Final Command, Mutation Surge and Wizard Abjuration use their printed next regular start. Momentum Barrier lasts one minute. A source with no specified shield endpoint uses the default.

King's Smite and Noble Bearing first resolve their shared internal component: when Noble applies, produce one Noble offer instead of a King's Smite offer. Each is half actual radiant Smite damage, rounded down, capped atS+M. Then compare that one offer with the recipient's existing shield. Their word “replaces” does not override an unrelated equal shield. Transfer-generated shields use the prior redirection package's actual absorbed amount, single-root restrictions and source caps; they appear after the causal packet and cannot retroactively protect it.

Each excess-healing point has one conversion owner. A source that explicitly converts its own excess has priority over external generic converters. Channel Life's packet forbids excess-to-temp-HP conversion by any provider; independent fixed shields still resolve normally. These are the existing healing interfaces, not a second excess pool.

## Druid: one body throughout

Keep your own HP, ability scores, saves, proficiency, conditions, personality and body identity. No copied monster statistics, separate beast HP or overflow pool exists. Base forms cannot speak; Arch/Hero forms can. Default size Medium, walking30, ordinary senses and operative character AC; change only the printed form traits. Hawk is Tiny; Bear, Earth Warden and Hero forms may be Large if legal space permits. No form invents hands or hand-based equipment use.

Equipment melds and cannot be used. **New AC bridge:** calculate `formNormalAC` from effects that remain operative in the form. Exclude worn armor's AC calculation, shield AC, effects requiring melded equipment use and unclassified item bonuses. A passive magical numeric item bonus requires the equipment adapter to certify anatomy compatibility. Apply the form's exact formula after that calculation, never adding worn armor again. Equipment returns in its prior state on reversion; shifting never repairs, reloads, restores charges or refreshes it. The full item/anatomy matrix remains unfinished.

Five Base forms unlock at1. Choose Circle at2; the chosen Circle's Arch path begins3, with its level6 feature. Circle Hero forms arrive at their printed10/14 gates. At11 attune at most two of the five Arch forms at a completed long rest. This is form acquisition, not another class promotion. All exact profiles and their complete original effects are in [the26-form register](../../data/playtest/druid_form_profiles.json).

At a completed long rest record:

- Shift uses2/3/4/5/6/7/8 at levels1/4/7/10/13/16/19. The conflicting historical schedule remains preserved.
- Buffer Reserve `2 × Druid level + M`.
- Form Surge Reserve `PB`.

These recorded reserves do not refill just because level, proficiency or form changes. At20 shift-use costs become zero, while Buffer Reserve, Surges and source-specific uses remain finite.

To enter a legal different profile, pay a Bonus Action and one shift use below20. End the previous instance and its dependent effects, create a fresh instance lasting10 minutes, clear Refrain's remembered spell/count, and retain Dissonance. Then resolve entry benefits. Bear offers `min(20, reserve)` and Earth Warden `min(30, reserve)`; deduct the whole offer even if a stronger shield wins. Both forms remain legal with reserve0. Natural attacks do not clear Refrain.

Early reversion costs a Bonus Action and no shift use; it does not clear Refrain. An early attempt to enter the already-current identical profile is rejected unpaid. At the exact natural10-minute endpoint, choosing to renew the same profile costs a shift use below20, with no new Bonus Action. Keep the same instance, local uses and existing effects; extend only the form endpoint. Do not refill its buffer, repeat entry effects, clear Refrain or extend a swarm/smoke effect's independent deadline. Declining renewal ends it normally. A later genuine reentry creates a new instance but cannot replenish shared reserves or per-rest abilities.

Elemental subtypes Air/Earth/Fire/Water and Vermin bat/ground choices are part of the profile identity. Switching subtype is a real new entry. Elemental entry additionally spends one of its two long-rest uses; natural renewal of the same subtype spends no new Elemental use. **New bounded profile completion:** Elemental attacks use lightning/bludgeoning/fire/cold respectively; Earth Warden's ordinary claw is slashing. An existing natural form attack without printed reach uses5 feet. These choices import no monster stat block.

## Attacks, specials and ending a form

One Action makes one printed natural attack, using currentPB+actualWIS and current Druid DC. A named Howl, Slam, Breath, summon, Smoke, Blast or Thunder Step replaces that Action's ordinary attack. Preserve each exact range, dice, save, condition and frequency. Natural/form attacks remain explicit categories; unrelated weapon-only procs are not authorized until the missing global taxonomy is reviewed. Expressly natural/form-qualified features such as Circle Forms and Primal Strike still work.

Local Surge use is keyed by actual form instance plus specific special. Legal commitment spends the opportunity and one Surge before rolls; miss/save/failure provides no refund. Mooncursed's ally and enemy Howls share one opportunity. Broodmother Spawn and critical-negation are separate opportunities, each requiring a Surge. Sky Serpent and Tempest's wet bonuses are attack riders, not extra attacks.

Broodmother's optional spawn exists only inside the entry transaction. A legal chosen spawn spends its Surge; an illegal or declined spawn spends none and does not undo entry. Once entry closes, there is no later spawn window for that instance. The separate critical-negation remains available. Carrion/Broodmother bodies use the reviewed creature profiles, independent lifetime and shared command budget; ending the parent instance ends them, while independent paid summons remain.

Earth Warden Slam's recharge2 belongs to the owner/source and persists across reversion/reentry. Tick only canonical regular starts or the protected six-second outside-initiative equivalent. Frost Breath's1/SR, Blazewood Blast's1/LR and Elemental entry's2/LR are likewise source/owner clocks, never form-instance refreshes.

The reference uses one `OwnerRechargeClock` timeline across both contexts. In initiative, actual regular starts consume due owner markers; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative, advancing actual elapsed time consumes the same six-second markers. Leaving and reentering initiative preserves the next due marker, so an elapsed tick and a turn start at that same boundary cannot count twice. Actual completed rests advance this downtime clock, allowing a two-round recharge to mature during the rest. Form changes themselves provide no ticks.

Mooncursed ally Howl: choose and order one to three legal allies before rolling a shared2d8. Sequentially offer `min(roll, reserve)` to each; deduct each entire offer before arbitration. Roll12 with reserve9 offers9,0,0. No voluntary under-offering or free redistribution. Zero creates no grant. A legal Howl at reserve0 still spends its Action, Surge and local opportunity. Its accepted ally shields survive form ending and expire by the ordinary recipient long-rest rule.

# Devices, Totems and companion commands

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED: 132 targeted checks and 1,200 reconfiguration states.** This is the lifecycle and shared-command overlay for 74 supplied Tinker/Shaman passages and three frozen shared paragraphs. It does not certify all effects on those cards, all companions, or the whole game.

The [source register](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) preserves all exact procedures and hashes. The [source check](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) and [behavior check](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) cover this bounded package. The other 157 passages in the wider companion inventory are still open. Original sources and the frozen class guide remain unchanged.

The original names, costs, targets, rolls, damage, class gates and frequencies control. A label such as “device,” “deployed” or “support command” below is a classification, not an added ability. **NEW** marks an integration decision explicitly discussed with the notebook.

## At the table

Keep one card/token for each active device, Totem or companion. Record its current HP, expiry, occupied capacity, spent ammunition/uses and protected disablement. A persistent Anacite Drone also retains an ownership identity across reconstruction.

When a device reaches 0 HP, release its active slot and record what destroyed it. A destroyed Drone remains a recoverable machine. Standard summoned companions disappear. Totems stop their aura immediately. Expiry, dismissal, replacement and loss of concentration end effects without producing destruction rewards.

Repair is not reconstruction. Field Repair and Repair Pulse cannot bring a destroyed machine back. Snap Rebuild and the Drone's ten-minute repair can do so under their exact costs, ranges and limits. Snap must still fit the original slot footprint and beat the original expiry.

All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and one damaging companion action per numbered round. Separate tokens, multiclass companions, an extra Action or an extra turn do not reset those limits.

## Lifecycle and persistent state

Primary state is deployed, retracted, destroyed, expired, ended or replaced. Protected disablement is a separate flag. A disabled Drone can be retracted or destroyed; neither action clears the flag. An active entity functions only while deployed, before its expiry, above 0 HP if it has HP, available in its owner's configuration, and not disabled.

**NEW:** administrative ending releases capacity without destruction, refunds or salvage. Earlier destruction debris can remain after the original timer, but cannot be Snap Rebuilt at or after that timer. Inert remnants do not acquire collision, cover, terrain or repair rights without a source.

The Drone has an asset identity for ownership and configuration and an instance identity for the current physical incarnation. Ordinary repair, retraction, redeployment, Snap and Reconfiguration preserve that instance. A genuinely new paid deployment or explicit long-rest Drone rebuild uses a new instance.

Protected disablement belongs to the persistent Drone asset. A long-rest rebuild can therefore produce a full-HP Drone that remains disabled. The printed automatic clearance is a completed **short rest**; a long rest is not silently substituted for that marker.

## Commands, Reactions and damage allowances

| Event | Shared BA command | Shared damaging action | Other payment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Attack command | Spent | Spent | Printed costs |
| Support-only command | Spent | Available | Printed costs |
| Gadget Sync shot | Unchanged | Spent | Trigger and 1 RP |
| Decoy Dummy destruction damage | Unchanged | Spent if available | Automatic engine trigger |
| Default follow/move/Dodge | Unchanged | Unchanged | No attack granted |
| Emergency Protocols, Protective Programming, Magnetic Wall | Unchanged | Unchanged | Owner's printed Reaction |
| Volatile Components / Cinderflame destruction burst | Unchanged | Unchanged | Their own predicates and limits |

Gadget Sync after support may use the still-unspent damaging allowance. Gadget Sync first leaves a later BA support command available. Neither sequence grants a second damaging activation. Rocket Tower's two-target shot is one activation; Advanced Turret Bay does not command both turrets together.

**NEW scope clarification:** engine[6]'s damaging-trigger limit applies to its deployable profiles, including Decoy. It does not impose that limit on separately printed Volatile Components or Cinderflame. A suppressed Decoy trigger grants no damage and is not banked. An off-turn Decoy trigger still uses the current numbered-round allowance. Tinker BA commands also require their narrower regular-turn eligibility. Other timing/trigger legality is checked by the caller.

Nano Aegis uses a support command for each printed BA+1RP output; it cannot attack with that command. Its reviewed maximum of three outputs remains. Duration extensions do not restore ammo, uses or healing pulses.

## Durability and immunities

| Profile | Maximum / initial HP | AC | Stat timing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anacite Drone | max(1, 5 + actual INT modifier + Tinker level) | 13 + actual INT modifier | Current actual owner values |
| Ordinary HP-bearing deployable | 2 × Tinker level | 12 + PB | NEW creation snapshot |
| Deployable Expertise on eligible object | Add M maximum/initial HP | Add 1 | Creation; excludes Drones |
| Totem, including Echo | 2 × Shaman level | 12 + PB | NEW placement snapshot |
| Named standard elemental | 2L; Harmony makes 3L | 12 + floor(PB/2) | Creation |
| Elemental Chorus package | 4L; Harmony makes 5L total | 12 + PB | Creation |
| Salvage / Reaper Scrapling | L | 12 | Creation |
| Restoration Field | No HP-bearing anchor | None | Slot effect |

A legitimate temporary actual INT change updates Drone AC, maximum HP and its current PB+INT attack bonus. Increased maximum supplies capacity without healing. Decreased maximum clamps current HP without damage or destruction. Finite created profiles keep their creation statistics.

Harmony adds HP at creation and one source turn of duration, capped at four. It does not heal an existing summon. Chorus is one shared package represented by four spirits. Echo's 10-foot radius and half aura numbers do not halve its durability.

Machines/Totem objects have no organic Wounds, Stable state or death saves. Legal temporary HP is a separate buffer. The Drone's printed poison/psychic and Charmed immunities do not imply every condition immunity. Totems have their own printed poison/psychic and condition immunities. “Vulnerable to ordinary weapon and other damage” means susceptible in this source wording, not an invented numerical doubling.

The reference's damage method receives an amount after all legally applicable defenses. Condition eligibility, object immunities, attack rolls, saves and exact riders remain caller work. A Shaman elemental is a creature companion, not automatically a machine.

Scraplings are temporary companions with their printed stats and shared command rules. Neither supplied Scrapling source establishes generic machine/device targeting. Salvage's slot cost does not grant that category. They disappear at zero HP and do not thereby gain Field Repair, Repair Pulse, protected-disable routing, Recycling, Volatile Components, Snap or other device-only permissions.

## Repair, reconstruction and disabling

| Procedure | Eligible target and change | Payment / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field Repair | Touched damaged machine with positive HP; or protected-disabled positive-HP machine, even at full HP. An available carried/retracted Drone qualifies. Restores rolled S d8+M up to max and clears protected disablement | Action, 1 RP, printed Recharge 2 |
| Repair Pulse | Up to three functional friendly devices; restores floor(maxHP/2), applies printed +1 AC until next source start. Does not clear protected disablement | Action, 3 RP, 1/short rest |
| Drone ten-minute reconstruction | Destroyed owned Drone with available original material; restores max(1, floor(maxHP/2)); preserves protected disablement | 10 minutes, 1 RP, 1/short rest |
| Snap Rebuild | Destroyed device/Drone, legal material, original free compatible slot footprint and remaining duration; restores max(1, floor(maxHP/2)); preserves disablement | BA, 2 RP, 1/encounter |
| Disable-clear tools procedure | Clears only protected-disable flag, including on a destroyed persistent machine; restores no HP | Separate 10 minutes, 1 RP, tinker's tools |
| Completed short rest | Clears protected disablement only | Actual completed short-rest marker |
| Long-rest Drone rebuild | Full HP, fresh physical instance for owned asset, even after old material consumed; preserves uncleared asset disablement | Actual source-authorized completed long rest |

**NEW machine viability arithmetic:** explicit half-maximum reconstruction has minimum 1 HP. Repair Pulse on a functional max-1-HP machine still restores floor(1/2) = 0.

The two ten-minute procedures are distinct rights. Reconstructing a disabled, destroyed Drone does not also buy disable clearance. Reconstruction is not a generic cleanse and does not reset ammunition, modules, spent uses, Overdrive history or unexpired legal effects. Normally damage has already consumed temp HP before destruction; this package adds no destroyed-machine temp-HP grant.

Routing Dissonance is the engine[7] BA, once/short rest, up to two current Dissonance into an active device within 30 feet. It creates no RP, does not reset Refrain, and blocks movement, attacks, auras and triggers while the device's timer continues.

## Capacity, placement and dependent Totems

Deployable slots are zero before the engine's class gate, one at Tinker 6, two at 13 and three at 17. Advanced Turret Bay uses two available slots for 4 RP, or its one-slot/2-RP fallback; zero free slots is illegal. Drones use separate persistent ownership capacity, not deployable slots.

At Tinker 13, choose exactly two basic Drones with exactly one module each or exactly one Drone with exactly two distinct modules during the printed configuration procedure. No more than two. Earlier module acquisition remains governed by its own class gates. **NEW:** withdrawing the excess Drone into an unavailable/retracted configuration causes no destruction or salvage.

Totem capacity is one, then two at Shaman 13. **NEW generalization:** an ordinary new Totem placed at capacity replaces a chosen active Totem, including at capacity one. Echo needs a separate free capacity; creating Echo alone never evicts another Totem.

**NEW dependent Echo rule:** ending, replacing, destroying or expiring the parent ends its Echo and releases both capacities. That Echo ending is administrative, not its own destruction. Ending only Echo leaves the parent. Echo shares the parent's remaining duration, concentration and upkeep.

Preflight ownership, source use, space/range, action, resources and capacity before payment or ending anything. Determine all dependent releases first. A valid parent replacement can free room for the new parent plus a separately paid Echo. If Echo cannot fit, its optional creation is unavailable; the caller can submit an ordinary parent-only placement instead. Failure of a submitted combined transaction changes nothing.

All active Totems share their concentration burden. Losing it ends their effects and dependent Echoes without destruction rewards. Totem movement follows its printed BA, 15-foot move through an open route within the printed range; it retains expiry, concentration, recipient ledgers and pulse schedule. Movement grants no entry heal.

## Destruction, debris and source-specific opportunities

Record the instance, original hostile cause, actual enemy hit versus transferred damage, deliberate sacrifice, whether the object itself is a copy, friendly damage, secondary explosion and inherited branch flags at destruction. Separately record whether incoming damage was copied. A real device destroyed by copied damage still has ordinary destruction consequences; only that damage's actual restriction flags suppress them. “Copied object” exclusions do not mean “any object damaged by a copy.”

**NEW anti-loop integration:** the first actual destruction of an instance establishes its only object-linked opportunity and material set. Nonqualifying and declined opportunities are closed for that instance. Snap does not create another set. A second physical destruction still ends the rebuilt device but cannot supply another harvest, Volatile opportunity or material record.

Recycling, Salvage, Reaper and Snap share the usable original material. The first successful consumer spends it. Volatile does not consume material. A source-qualified Volatile can therefore precede one legal material consumer. Declining Volatile on Device A does not spend the owner's round allowance for Device B.

| Source | Important predicate |
| --- | --- |
| Efficient Recycling | Your destroyed non-copy device; not deliberate sacrifice; debris within reach, after combat for one minute, 1/short rest. Refund at most min(1 RP, actual deployment RP). Enemy cause is **not required**. |
| Scrap Salvage | Enemy-destroyed qualifying material; Action+1 RP, 1/encounter; one slot-using Scrapling at printed location |
| Scrap Reaper | Qualifying destroyed enemy-hit device/material within 30 feet; Reaction+2 RP, 1/short rest; printed short-lived Scrapling uses **no deployable slot** |
| Volatile Components | First enemy-caused device destruction; excludes deliberate sacrifice, copy, friendly damage and secondary explosion; enemy within 5 feet; once per owner/round |
| Snap | Original destroyed instance/material, original footprint free and original expiry not reached |

Scraplings cannot spawn their own replacement. Reaper still uses the later BA command and damaging-action budget for its detonation. Its absent slot cost is not inferred from the separate Salvage card. Reaper also carries its source's broader no-own-destruction-chain property; a later type ruling must not silently remove that protection.

Inherited noResourceGeneration blocks Recycling refunds. It does not automatically prohibit all non-resource transformations. Inherited noRetaliation blocks a destruction explosion such as Volatile. Inherited noDeathTriggers blocks Volatile, Cinder's destruction burst and Reaper's destruction-triggered Reaction. It does not automatically prohibit the later Action-based Scrap Salvage or ordinary Recycling. Source-specific exclusions still apply to each consumer.

Cinderflame's qualifying destruction event is captured before its standard-companion disappearance. Its printed burst may then resolve, with the printed three-enemy cap, save, damage and no further death/resource triggers. Dismissal, expiry and concentration ending are not destruction.

Volatile Injection spends M **normal** device HP and requires current HP strictly greater than M. Temp HP cannot pay it. It is not damage or a qualifying destruction event. Deliberate sacrifice sources retain their express no-proc/salvage/copy/refund exclusions.

## Magnetic Wall and existing damage sharing

**NEW source binding and timing integration:** when the printed ranged weapon hit, ally distance and wall-line predicates hold, the owner's Reaction transfers exactly min(remaining defended damage, S+M) to the functional Wall after the ally's ordinary defenses/prevention and before temp HP.

The transfer retains damage type. The Wall branch carries noSecondMitigation and noRetransfer. It receives no second AC roll, critical, attack-hit rider or second mitigation pass. Legal Wall temp HP then normal HP absorb it; reaching zero destroys it and releases its slot.

Enemy damage intercepted this way remains enemy-caused. Choosing the Reaction is not deliberate sacrifice. A Wall destroyed this way may qualify Volatile and a source-qualified material consumer. Transferred damage is not itself an attack hit on the Wall; enemy-hit-only Reaper qualification remains distinct.

Emergency Protocols retains its existing additional noRetaliation flag. Enemy attribution and ordinary debris survive, but destroying the Drone cannot bypass that flag to trigger Volatile. This new Magnetic Wall binding supplements the earlier 39-source redirection package; it was not part of that package's original count.

## Reconfiguration and implementation boundaries

Reconfiguration requires a functional deployed device and a known eligible nonhealing destination. **NEW arithmetic:** newHP = max(1, floor(oldHP × newMaxHP / oldMaxHP)), capped at new max. Preserve instance, slot footprint, expiry, ammunition, spent uses, destruction history and effect clocks. This conversion is neither damage nor healing.

Pending modifiers only apply when their own predicate remains true. Overcharge grants no free command; a profile unable to use it does not refund it or reset its deadline. Exact source access, profile legality and pending-modifier application remain caller responsibilities.

Restoration Field is a slot-using concentration effect with its already-reviewed healing scheduler. Its source supplies no HP, AC or physical anchor. It cannot be attacked as a fabricated machine, repaired, Snap Rebuilt, Remote Detonated, used for Volatile Injection/salvage or targeted by protected Dissonance routing merely because it consumes a slot.

The implementation stores authoritative owner/instance/material identifiers, original ClockMarkers, canonical command ledgers, atomic RP/action payments and explicit source-scoped use keys. The caller must provide the same real owner wallet and ledger across abilities, unique use-scope keys tied to the real rest/encounter calendar, legal source actions and costs, actual targets/geometry, source profiles and class gates. It must also propagate these life states to the pulse/concentration engine.

All timed device effects supplied here expire during a completed long rest, explaining the fresh Drone instance's empty timed-effect list and zero tempHP. This is not a generic reconstruction cleanse: a future permanent or long-rest-surviving source effect must retain its own clock and rules.

This reference does not create a complete runtime transaction manager, movement/collision system, all damage riders, every condition interaction, all 157 remaining companion candidates or a video game. It supplies the same decisions in tabletop prose and a precise checked model for later implementation.

## Discussion evidence

Saved in docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game:

# Time Loop: reviewed foundational transaction kernel

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the bounded foundational scope. Full Time Loop remains unavailable.**

**Current-file qualification:** the original approval binds helper hash `b821829ed352e69ce1ecf3c3d753f0206c8f8d2ec5a5d64bc89d5fd7d8a72151`, preserved as `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/temporal_playtest_rules_reviewed_foundation.py` at the game root. The current helper adds a control/pulse transaction adapter and regular-start phase tracking. Those extensions are now covered by the separate [bounded control/pulse review manifest](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_REVIEW_STATUS.json), following actual notebook confirmation. They do not inherit the historical approval. The 76 foundation regressions still pass. See [integration progress](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_PLAYTEST.md).

This implements a bounded part of `oracle.supplement.spiral-touched.spiral-touched-boon-v`. It does not change the original source, enable the ability in the playable class catalog, or close the full temporal interface. The notebook's twelve decisions are the authority for this candidate: [boundary conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_WORLD_BOUNDARIES.md).

## What is implemented

The reference restores an immutable initiative-start snapshot through a preflighted transaction. It handles a finite development scene containing canonical Core life states, action wallets, selected feat shields, a temporal healing-consumption ledger, explicit Soul Bind/death identities, physical provenance, finite level-ground geometry, reward opportunities, external dependency records and character memory. The existing shared `LifeState`, `Wallet` and `BufferLedger` objects retain their identities. Spent resources and historical event records remain current.

The restore is permitted only after a complete atomic combat event, before round four, with an available Reaction and an unspent actual long-rest use. It never interrupts a damage, healing or command transaction. Preflight checks all registered state, source policies, physical dependencies and placements before charging anything. A prepared plan becomes stale if the registered world changes before commit. The single-thread reference requires the host scene lock through preflight and commit. Each committed restore also retains an engine/Director audit frame with the previous and resulting field values; that audit is never a source of character memory. The existing canonical BufferLedger completed-rest epoch also governs Time Loop's own long-rest use; there is no independent rest counter to diverge.

At commit, encounter initiative and the snapshot's Action/Bonus Action/Reaction allowances, RC and declared per-encounter uses return. Every outstanding Oracle Time Loop Reaction debt overlays the restored budgets. Only the owner's actual normal regular-start refresh clears that owner's debt. The public `TemporalKernel.regular_start(actor, now)` obtains the actor's canonical Wallet internally; it accepts no Wallet argument and rejects actor aliases sharing one Wallet. The bounded scheduler enforces the next actor at the initiative cursor, allows one active regular turn, and advances the cursor/round only when that exact turn ends. An out-of-order or repeated start cannot refresh a Reaction or advance the actual regular marker. Genuine extra turns require the later source adapter and cannot be represented as regular starts. The new iteration has fresh round/turn identities; the rewind itself creates no turn start, pulse or recharge tick. Elapsed world time, real regular-marker count, RP and finite-use history remain unchanged.

## Conservation checks

| State | Bounded behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Core HP and Wounds | Restore numeric snapshot HP against the current legal maximum. A lower maximum clamps HP without damage or healing; a higher maximum does not increase snapshot HP. Critical Wound healing ceilings do not limit temporal assignment. |
| Maximum HP | Use the existing maximum-HP calculation and an exact source-ID temporal policy table. The three reviewed Monk trauma IDs may restore except after actual rest ending. Tough, Tough as Nails, Tenacity and Dark Fortitude use current permanent progression records; temporary endpoints on those passive records are rejected. Other sources, including valid ordinary max-HP sources whose temporal/lifecycle adapter is absent, reject this fixture. Current supported external records overlay the result. Structural progression changes reject without a dedicated adapter. The host supplies current legal base/stat values. |
| Stable recovery | Preserve its original world deadline and event identity. An already resolved or expired recovery cannot replay; this kernel rejects such restoration rather than inventing a recovery rule. |
| Temporary HP | Restore the same grant ID and original snapshot amount only while its source's deadline/rest epoch/entity dependency remains valid. Supported IDs are Chef, Inspiring Leader, Field Medic, Soul Cage, Empowered Summoning and Blood Ritual. Required canonical ledger fields, unique grant IDs, active target/state and positive remaining amount are validated. Unknown sources and linked riders reject the scene. |
| One-shot healing reduction | Keep canonical effect ID and all past events. Consumption keys include the iteration. Snapshot-available Agony can be available in a new iteration before its original expiry; snapshot-consumed or expired Agony remains unavailable. |
| Soul Bind | Original absolute deadline, exact death instance for bound-dead records. An active pending record requires a living, non-Stable, dying zero-HP target with no death-instance binding. Application and target identities must match. Undoing a later death removes that later active bind. No revival event or source cost is manufactured. |
| Rewards | A claim belongs to encounter origin, immutable reward source, opportunity kind and source-defined slot. Another death event or iteration cannot make another claim. |
| Physical derivatives | Traverse immutable provenance transitively. A wholly in-scope, reversible temporal entity can retire; its costs stay spent. Surviving harvested inventory, mixed material roots, external source slots or persistent enrollment conflicts block the restore. Already consumed material remains consumed. |
| Outsiders | Keep body state, inventory ownership, resource history and concentration records. A snapshot dependency must still exist exactly and refer to the same live concentration ID. New current dependencies targeting restored participants need a supported overlay; otherwise they block. Unimplemented external anatomy/control/suppression overlays also block. |
| Environment | Each anchor has an exact canonical physical identity. Restore snapshot environment existence together with its geometry; remove both the physical derivative and its geometry when retiring a later temporal entity. Plan all participant positions simultaneously. Reject overlap, loss of support, and restrictions to a protected outsider's previously reachable ground area. This is deliberately limited to a finite orthogonal level ground plane, not flying, elevation, portals or mandatory growth. |
| Memory | The invoking Oracle and their immutable snapshot allies retain only facts individually perceived, experienced or received. Retained memories accumulate across loops. Enemy player characters receive no special knowledge; no hidden roster or Director facts enter memory automatically. |

## What the agreed rules mean at the table

These examples explain the reviewed boundaries. They do not enable the full ability before its remaining integrations are complete.

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| At initiative, an ally has25HP. Later they fall to3HP and spend8RP. Time Loop succeeds. | They return to25HP, limited by their current legal maximum. The8RP remain spent. Their snapshot encounter allowances return where the source explicitly permits it. |
| The same ally's legal maximum has fallen to20 because a conserved source changed. | They return to20HP. The reduction is temporal normalization, not damage or healing, and creates neither Wounds nor resource triggers. A structural progression change without its adapter instead makes the restore unavailable. |
| An ally began with a6-point Soul Cage shield, later lost it, and the original grant remains valid. | The same shield returns with its snapshot6 points. The Soul Charge paid for it remains spent. This is not a new cast, grant or recipient offer. |
| Oracle A uses Time Loop. Before A's next actual regular turn, Oracle B uses it too. | Both Oracles retain their Reaction debts. Rewinding does not clear A's debt. Each debt clears only at that Oracle's genuine normal Reaction refresh. |
| A restored enemy dies again after its reward opportunity was already claimed. | That same reward cannot be claimed again. The source opportunity, rather than the new death event, determines whether it was paid. |
| A body part was harvested after initiative and still exists as somebody else's item. | The generic restore is unavailable: it cannot duplicate the body part or take away the current owner's item. A specifically reviewed reconciliation would be required. |
| An ally saw a hidden passage in the discarded timeline; another ally never learned about it. | The witness can retain that memory if eligible through the invoking Oracle's snapshot alliance. The other ally receives no automatic knowledge. The witness can tell them normally. |

An unavailable restore spends neither the Reaction nor the long-rest entitlement. The Director needs a complete, legal proposed state before resolving the ability; unresolved source interactions cannot be waived by calling a snapshot complete.

## Required integrations still missing

The minimum seventeen-domain review is not complete. `TemporalKernel.support_report()` reports that limit. `playable_plan()` always rejects until the full implementation and independent review exist. `kernel_plan()` is a development fixture interface, not a replacement for the complete Oracle feature. # Time Loop: control and healing-pulse integration

**Bounded live control/pulse transaction interface jointly reviewed and reference-validated. Full Time Loop remains unavailable.**

The [actual nine-part conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_CONTROL_PULSE_BOUNDARIES.md) supplements the [twelve world-conservation decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_WORLD_BOUNDARIES.md). The existing [control](CONTROL_STATES_PLAYTEST.md) and [pulse](HEALING_PULSE_PLAYTEST.md) guides continue to own ordinary source behavior. No original card was changed.

## Agreed temporal behavior

| State | Temporal rule |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit source/target regular endpoints | Restore remaining logical progress with authentic new-iteration regular markers. World elapsed time does not move backward, and restoration creates no marker event. |
| Current actual-turn endings | Remain attached to the actual application turn. The initiative-start snapshot has no active turn; a pending in-turn attachment there is invalid. Outside-turn +6-second endpoints retain their absolute deadline. |
| Outside-origin pulse schedules | Keep their original virtual markers and absolute deadlines. Entering initiative or using Time Loop does not restart them. Origin must be recorded explicitly. |
| Speed records | Same application, exact source/component/profile and valid endpoint. Do not reapply or refresh. Current external suppression remains authoritative. Aura, net, form, serum and creature children require their actual parent adapters. Hypermutation's floor is systemic parent state, not a hostile slow. |
| Guiding Bolt's Star mark | Restore its two separate entitlements. Keep the same mark identity and monotonic attack-token history; pending attacks block capture and preflight. |
| Wrathful Brand | Restore the separate owner/ally riders and snapshot timed parent. No new damage, healing or save event occurs at restore. |
| One-shot riders | Use exact parent/application/source/component identities and a finite trigger table. Vein Cutter consumes on its qualifying attack hit; Crippling Lash specifically requires a weapon hit. Omen Reader's once/encounter attack adjustment is distinct from the resulting timed star-ash. |
| Divine Judgment reflection | Retain historical actual-turn consumption. A genuinely new iteration turn can qualify, including a separately authenticated extra turn. Ordinary repeat saves and expiry still use regular markers. |
| PulseSeries | Restore snapshot pending/funded/consumed state under the same valid parent and fixed roster. No cast pulse or consumed-at-snapshot opportunity replays. A later pending paid pulse pays its current printed cost when actually due. |
| Recipient budgets | Retain history with domain, target and iteration-round identity. Circle of Harmony remains shared across owners in the same iteration-round. |
| Eternal Bloom | Preserve the original missing-HP capture and shares. Restore only snapshot installment availability; retain old consumption history. Do not grow the reserve from later damage. Its survival floor is separate. |
| First-contact cures | Restore snapshot instance/recipient entitlements. Garden uses entry/start; Enhanced Garden and Seed use their reviewed pulse event. Restore itself is none of these events. Real-rest recipient histories remain conserved. |
| Native healing | One evaluated opportunity at a genuine regular start during a real encounter. Decline, ineligibility or unavailable payment loses that start opportunity. Extra turns and downtime create no tick. A new iteration can supply a new genuine start, with current RP/reserves. |

**Resource-output conservation:** Transcendent Meditation's second pulse can supply1Ki only once for the same effect instance. Sacred Chant's third pulse can supply1Conviction only once for that instance. Reaching the occurrence while capped or while the whole effect is suppressed still consumes that resource opportunity. Healing may later replay under an authorized restored source without generating the same resource again. A never-reached opportunity remains eligible. Restoration itself grants neither resource.

For example, a Monk receives the second pulse's1Ki, then spends it. Rewinding to a snapshot where that pulse was pending can permit its healing again when legally due, but it cannot return that same1Ki. Sacred Chant uses the same conservation rule for Conviction.

The immutable snapshot is at initiative start. A source first created afterward is not silently added to that snapshot. An origin label cannot manufacture preexisting pulse state. Any logical-clock restoration must demonstrate that the actual source instance was already present in the captured state.

The conference's maintenance wording is read with its express instruction not to reopen ordinary mechanics: an early failed ordinary turn-window payment remains pending until the source's real turn-end deadline. Exact-due paid sequences/windows end immediately on failed upkeep. The notebook explicitly [confirmed this distinction and immutable snapshot membership](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PULSE_BRIDGE_CLOSURE.md). No currently supplied pulse profile needs a fabricated at-initiative creation exception; native passive abilities instead await their future genuine regular-start events.

## Current code and checks

`tools/temporal_control_playtest_rules.py` currently implements two limited bridges:

- `CanonicalPulseWallet` lets existing pulse helpers spend the real actor Wallet's RP/Bonus Action and the canonical Scheduler's RC. It owns no duplicate balances and rejects changed aliases before spending.
- `ConservedPulseOutputs` wraps actual `PulseSeries.resolve()` calls for the two resource-producing profiles. It retains unique occurrence IDs and conserved instance/index/component opportunities; it replaces the helper's raw Ki flag with the guarded allowance. Suppressed or capped resolved occurrences cannot be banked. Sacred Chant cannot generate Conviction outside a real encounter.

The returned resource allowance must be applied once by the host in the same atomic event, subject to the actual resource cap. These helpers do not themselves own, increment or restore Ki/Conviction. Source acquisition, legal recipients, actual parent concentration and authenticated due-event scheduling remain host/source-adapter responsibilities. The output guard cannot certify them.

[Validation](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_VALIDATION.json):22 focused methods pass. They exercise the actual existing maintenance, Song, Meditation, Chant and native payment interfaces, plus duplicate output, cap, suppression, early/duplicate occurrence and canonical-alias cases. A replay test deliberately resets only an isolated series view; it demonstrates the output guard, not a complete Time Loop source restoration. The [actual independent review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_PULSE_BRIDGE_CLOSURE.md) approves only these payment/resolved-output bridges. The [review manifest](TEMPORAL_PULSE_BRIDGE_REVIEW_STATUS.json) binds that approval to the exact unchanged helper. The validation JSON retains its original submitted pre-review scope label as evidence; the separate review manifest records the later disposition.

## Still required

The `tools/temporal_control_world.py` integration passes 50 methods, alongside the 76 foundation and 22 payment/output methods. The [actual notebook closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_CLOSURE.md) confirms the bounded interface after four review rounds. Its [review manifest](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_REVIEW_STATUS.json) binds the exact helper, tests and foundation extension; it does not transfer this approval to future edits. It restores selected same-object fields, watches aliases and current concentration callbacks, preserves original outside-origin pulse clocks, and uses authenticated regular-start phases. Hemostasis uses the target's start; other admitted sequences use the source's. Bloom installments and pulse-triggered contacts require current parent occurrence receipts. Native optional healing records an evaluated start even when declined, ineligible or unaffordable.

The repaired world requires the host's existing `ConservedPulseOutputs` guard as an explicit constructor argument. It delegates resource-producing pulses to that same guard and watches its canonical bindings, consumption and event history in the restore transaction. There is no second independent-output ledger. Child operations reject a parent whose clock projection reveals missed upkeep. Capture rejects participant recipient-round claims until a real outside-round import adapter exists. Unclassified Speed suppression blocks capture/restore. Prepared plans also watch the concentration object's complete schema. Eternal Bloom and Crown Restored require concentration through the existing `oracle.engine[26]` zone rule; prepaid Final pulses do not waive that requirement.

Capture now checks that an active pulse already existed and remains live at the actual snapshot marker, without mutating it. Every pulse, installment, contact and native component has an exact admitted identifier. The adapter validates mutable collection types before resource/occurrence writes. When original outside-clock Bloom opportunities are already past, their shares are lost without healing; the installment cursor advances past them so a later authentic due installment can still resolve. No original missing-HP reserve or share is recomputed.

Snapshot concentration bindings include the actual owner, concentration ID, slot object and callback object. Retained references prevent identity-token reuse. A same-ID replacement, even with the same callback or subsequently registered components, rejects before writes. This preserves the original later-ending callback; it does not restore ended/replaced concentration.

This is still bounded component code. Exact supplied source/target schedules and source eligibility remain host inputs; original outside-initiative round-ledger import is not implemented. The new integration does not execute complete cards or apply HP/Ki/Conviction output to final life/resource holders. It admits only the explicit control policy rows and three paid native sources. Omen Reader, extra turns, movement/entry receipts, mutation reserves, shared multi-parent contact holders, device/stasis/copy parents and complete source sibling lifecycles remain unsupported. Missing or ended required concentration rejects restoration. Parent retirement/restoration beyond the existing exact callback is not implemented.

Complete nine-family/source restoration remains in progress. No supported-adapter count or ordinary catalog status has been promoted. Required work includes complete source clock/parent adapters, final resource/output application, complete shared recipient history across initiative boundaries, and the outstanding lifecycles above. [Validation](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_VALIDATION.json) and the bounded approval do not certify full Time Loop.

Rapid Coagulation additionally needs the canonical previous-turn movement baseline from the initiative snapshot. It remains unsupported until that state exists. Net Bolt, Totem/Echo, Nano-Aegis, auras and other dependent sources remain unavailable to Time Loop without their physical/device/parent adapters. The seven major integrations and final whole-game/GitHub gate remain open.

## Object damage and Sunder

These are **new mundane object procedures** completing the Core Sunder interface. A target must be one actual separately tracked object or explicitly modeled separable component. Naming an armor strap, pin, lace, hinge or seam does not create a cheaper independent target. Construct joints remain subject to the creature's actual stat block.

Sunder uses an actual legal weapon attack against one perceived reachable object/component, consuming one attack when taking the Attack Action. It grants no extra attack or free damage to a wearer. The attacker cannot target a hidden component through a creature or solid obstruction. Against worn/held gear, target AC is the higher of the material AC and wearer's current AC. Unattended gear uses material AC. Ordinary attack eligibility and printed object-target exclusions still apply.

Worn/carried inventory is never damaged merely because its creature is hit. An attack, spell or hazard damages equipment only if its actual rule expressly targets/includes objects, structures, carried gear or that item. Sunder never also damages the wearer unless another source expressly says so.

| Load-bearing material | AC |
|---|---:|
| Cloth, paper, rope | 11 |
| Glass, crystal | 13 |
| Wood, leather | 15 |
| Stone | 17 |
| Iron, steel | 19 |

For a mixed object, establish its dominant load-bearing material before damage. Do not retroactively select a material after the attack roll.

| Mundane object | Maximum structural HP |
|---|---:|
| Tiny vial or letter | 1 |
| Tool, weapon or focus | 5 |
| Ordinary shield | 10 |
| Tower shield | 15 |
| Light armor | 10 |
| Medium armor | 15 |
| Heavy armor | 20 |
| Ordinary chest or door | 20 |
| Cart | 30 |
| Targeted rope segment | 5 |
| Targeted chain segment | 10 |

Large-sized wearable/item generic HP doubles; Crude armor's half-HP rule then applies. Specific source/card durability wins, including a net's AC 10/5 slashing destruction rule and Tinker gnome devices' AC 5/HP 1. The ordinary buckler is a shield using 10 generic HP. Objects outside a listed or genuinely comparable category need an actual assigned profile before targeted durability resolution; no automatic structure or artifact certification is implied.

Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage unless an exact rule says otherwise. Establish physical damage compatibility before rolling: a sword cannot chop a liquid. Do not invent retroactive resistances. Use ordinary attack damage and applicable weapon properties; creature-only conditions and resource triggers do not become object-eligible.

At zero structural HP, the object is **Broken** and loses usable AC, weapon, focus, tool or other functional benefits. It still exists, occupies its hand/slot/container and retains mass until dropped, removed or repaired. Broken armor does not disappear. No negative HP, duplicated loot, automatic explosion, passive regeneration or repair from ordinary rest. Magic items/artifacts need their own durability; no mundane default is assigned to unresolved magical gear. True Polymorph's independently excluded-object rules still apply even when an object has HP.

A Broken item grants none of its positive usable benefits, but remains physically worn, held or strapped until removed. It continues to occupy its hand/slot and contribute weight/Load, and retains physical drawbacks from still wearing or carrying it: applicable don/doff requirements, armor Stealth disadvantage, STR-minimum movement penalty and nonproficiency consequences. A Broken shield grants no AC bonus but still occupies its actual hand/forearm until doffed. A specific source may state otherwise.
